title: The Curious Learner (sample)
description: A made-up book for testing the app. It explains simple study habits in short chapters.

discover_cards.title: The curiosity gap
discover_cards.front: We want to learn most when we notice a small gap between what we know and what we want to know.
discover_cards.back: Asking a question before reading opens that gap on purpose.

discover_cards.title: Start with a question
discover_cards.front: A good question is a hook: the answer has something to hold on to.
discover_cards.speaker: Ada Sample

discover_cards.title: The 10% brain myth
discover_cards.front: We only use 10% of our brains.
discover_cards.back: Brain scans show activity all over the brain during a normal day; no large part sits unused.

discover_cards.title: The forgetting curve
discover_cards.front: Memory fades fast after learning, and each review makes it fade more slowly.
discover_cards.back: The picture shows three drops in memory, each one gentler after a review.
discover_cards.media_alt: A line chart: a curve falls quickly, then restarts higher twice, each time falling more slowly.

discover_cards.title: Testing yourself
discover_cards.front: Trying to remember something makes the memory stronger than reading it again.
discover_cards.back: Close the book and write what you remember, then check.

discover_cards.title: Learning styles
discover_cards.front: People learn best when lessons match their personal learning style.
discover_cards.back: Studies that tested this found no benefit from matching lessons to a preferred style.

discover_cards.title: Sleep keeps what you learned
discover_cards.front: During sleep the brain replays and stores what you learned that day.
discover_cards.back: A night of sleep after studying helps more than an extra hour of study.

discover_cards.title: Mix your practice
discover_cards.front: Mixing different kinds of problems feels harder but teaches you to choose the right method.
discover_cards.back: Practise A, B, C, A, C, B instead of A, A, A, B, B, B.

discover_cards.title: Small steps
discover_cards.front: Ten minutes today beats an hour someday.
discover_cards.speaker: Ada Sample

discover_cards.title: Teach it to learn it
discover_cards.front: Explaining an idea to someone else shows you which parts you do not understand yet.
discover_cards.back: Try explaining it in plain words to a friend, or to an empty chair.

practice_cards.prompt: Why does testing yourself help you remember?
practice_cards.answer: Pulling a memory out makes it stronger than reading it again.

practice_cards.prompt: Which way of studying builds the strongest memory?
choices: Closing the book and recalling it
practice_cards.explanation: Recalling from memory is a test, and tests strengthen memories.

practice_cards.prompt: Reading a text twice helps more than trying to recall it once.
practice_cards.explanation: Trying to recall it helps more.

practice_cards.prompt: Most of the brain is unused on a normal day.
practice_cards.explanation: Activity shows up all over the brain.

practice_cards.prompt: Put this mixed practice plan in the order the chapter suggests.
Match each learning habit with what it does.
practice_cards.explanation: Recall strengthens memories, sleep stores them, and mixed problems practise choosing a method.

practice_cards.prompt: Match each idea with what it means.
match_right: Noticing what you do not know yet
Explaining an idea to find your weak spots
